speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Last year, I wore green in this House during our debate on sustainability and the environment, and I have literally gone green by painting my face and my hands completely green to show how serious Nee Soon is in cutting our carbon emissions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Do not worry, Sir, I promise I will not be painting my face or hands during this speech.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As we keep getting greener, let us also not forget the other important colour – blue.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Today, Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin and I will be speaking up for our blue nature spaces.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I will be calling for greater protection for our marine spaces and Ms Samdin will be focusing on one of our other important blue spaces – the Southern Islands.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These numbers may continue to increase as we discover and rediscover more species.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Neptune's Cup Sponge, thought to be globally extinct, was rediscovered near St John's Island in 2011.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Just last year, we discovered three new species of moss animals in the Sisters' Islands Marine Park.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am glad that the Government is joining the world in protecting this rich biodiversity.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Singapore has committed to contribute to these global targets and I am glad that, once again, Singapore is playing a role as a responsible international party.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The second reason our marine ecosystems are important is climate change.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Marine ecosystems trap carbon and keep it from worsening climate change.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Mangroves also help in adaptation efforts against sea level rise and coral reefs reduce wave energy.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Such nature-based solutions against climate change can provide over one-third of the mitigation needed to achieve net-zero by 2050.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They need to be part of our roadmap to net zero.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: To help these marine ecosystems to be our swords and shields against climate change, we should protect them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: How can we further protect our marine spaces?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have three proposals to learn more, protect more and restore what we have lost.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These are not my ideas but what our young researchers and activists, Sam Shu Qin, Inez Alsagoff and Samantha Thian are calling for.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many of our marine advocates are up in the gallery.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The first proposal is to learn more about our marine spaces.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We have many passionate scientists who are studying our marine spaces.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She is a coral scientist who has been actively studying our coral reefs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Scientists like Sam are working hard to study our marine spaces.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, there remain gaps in our knowledge and they need the Government's support to continue and intensify their work.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Our last marine biodiversity survey was in 2015.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The last edition of the Singapore Red Data Book List on species in Singapore was in 2008.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Our database of knowledge is due for an update.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope that the Government can provide support to and work with researchers to update and plug gaps in our existing knowledge on our marine ecosystems.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In addition to her research work, Sam co-founded “Our Singapore Reefs”, which connects marine enthusiasts through diving and raises awareness on marine biodiversity through outreach programmes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She tells me, “I envision a future where we can all work hand in hand to create spaces where wildlife can co-exist with humans.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Together with our research, conservation and community initiatives, we can better safeguard our native biodiversity and keep our ecosystems healthy with more legislation, funding support and long-term partnership from the Government.” The second proposal is that as we learn more about our marine spaces, we also take steps to protect these spaces.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We should designate more marine areas as nature reserves or marine parks.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Nature spaces that are designated as nature reserves, national parks or public parks enjoy protection under the Parks and Trees Act.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Nature reserves and national parks get the most protection.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Any changes to their boundaries can only be amended after debate in Parliament.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But public parks like marine parks do not enjoy the same level of protection.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Their boundaries can be redrawn without the scrutiny of Parliament.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In 2001, the Government had already finalised plans to reclaim the Chek Jawa wetlands.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This unique habitat – home to mudskippers, dugongs, herons and otters – was on the verge of being destroyed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But these plans were suspended only after activists commissioned a biodiversity survey, wrote their own report and submitted a petition to the Government.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But we should not protect our marine spaces only when ordinary people take extraordinary action.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As our first marine park, the Sisters’ Islands Marine Park should receive more protection by elevating it to a nature reserve.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope we can designate these areas as marine parks first before subsequently considering them to be nature reserves.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These waters are familiar to Inez, who is an avid diver and a nature guide.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She shared this with me: “As a frequent diver, I have had the opportunity to conduct research with NUS and explore Singapore's Southern Islands.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I have witnessed first-hand the remarkable biodiversity present in our waters, including sightings of blacktip reef sharks, blue-spotted fantail rays, large groupers and vibrant coral ecosystems.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I strongly believe that we need to take action to protect our marine spaces and ensure their conservation for future generations.” The third proposal is that we go beyond protecting what we have to restoring what we have lost.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Our community of activists is working hard on the ground to protect our marine spaces.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Samantha Thian, who founded Seastainable, is one such activist.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Seastainable is a social enterprise supporting marine conservation in the region.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: On seeing the amount of trash and pollution on our beaches, Samantha started a Telegram group to organise beach clean-ups, gathering hundreds of volunteers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This has now grown to thousands of clean-ups.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While our local community works hard to protect our beaches, I hope the Government can match their efforts a little further from the beach.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We can start by restoring our degraded seagrass meadows.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Currently, the Tropical Marine Science Institute is studying the restoration of marine habitats such as seagrass meadows.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While seagrass may not receive as much attention as coral reefs, they are crucial as carbon sinks, home to rich biodiversity, improve water quality and protect our coast.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: They are also nurseries to fishes and feed marine creatures such as parrotfishes, turtles and dugongs.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is critical that we not just protect but restore our degraded seagrass meadows.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The largest meadows today are found at Chek Jawa, Pulau Semakau and Cyrene Reef.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: There are also substantial meadows in the waters of Pulau Pawai, Labrador Beach, Pasir Ris Beach, Changi Beach and Pulau Sekudu.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope the Government can support efforts to restore seagrass meadows in these areas.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Activists had proposed comprehensive recommendations to maintain and conserve our local marine environment.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: To conclude, Sir, I hope that we can respond to the calls of our young advocates to know our marine ecosystems better, protect what we currently have and restore what we have lost, especially our seagrass meadows.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These proposals level the playing field for nature when it comes to development decisions and give our wildlife in our waters a chance at survival.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In doing so, we also increase humankind’s chances of survival.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I saw the amazing biodiversity we were about to destroy at Chek Jawa and it was painful to see what we were going to lose.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I also saw first-hand the tremendous dedication by the researchers, activists and thousands of people, members of the public who stepped forward to speak up and fight for the protection of Chek Jawa.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And I also saw how the Government responded positively, reversed our decision and protected Chek Jawa instead.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I hope we continue to support our researchers and activists, continue to protect our marine spaces and continue to save our nature areas.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If the sea is sick, we'll feel it.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Our future and the state of the ocean are one."

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Over the years, like you, I have had the opportunity to volunteer as a clean-up diver and kayaked around our waters.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While what is under the surface may not always be front of mind, my time out on and in our waters has made me determined to play my part in our collective action.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The Southern Islands refer to a cluster of islands, an informal planning area to the south of mainland Singapore.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It comprises Kusu, Lazarus, Seringat, St John's, Sentosa, Tekukor and the two Sisters' islands.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For some time, visitors were generally marine scientists, casual picnickers, Kusu pilgrims, nostalgic former islanders or those in search of a trail off the beaten track.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Together with some marine scientists and environmental advocates, I toured the exhibition and was interested in how the LTPR highlighted the creation of an island of "green, blue and fun" by expanding nature-based recreation networks and embracing islandness.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This includes plans to transform our Southern Islands.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While it is exciting to hear new plans and see Singaporeans engaged in these nature spaces, the Southern Islands must be developed sensitively.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Given that the Southern Islands are more or less a blank slate, it would be exciting as well to testbed sustainable ideas and the learnings could be implemented on mainland Singapore.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some may wonder what is there to protect in the first place.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The Southern Islands are significant in two key areas: natural and cultural heritage.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The Southern Islands support coastal habitats to several nationally vulnerable or endangered species.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is also home to a rich culture and history.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The islands were part of the lively settlements of Orang Laut and former islanders have religious significance and hosted Singapore's first quarantine centre – when we are talking about COVID-19 today.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Given the natural and cultural significance of the Southern Islands, I appreciate the efforts of NParks, which engages and consults stakeholders and URA for adopting a science-based approach to stewarding green and blue spaces through the ecological profiling exercise (EPE).

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The EPE showed that the Southern Islands is a space where development should be considered sensitively.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Based on these findings, I ask that we consider how best to ensure the careful integration of conservation and development in our plans.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In recent times, we have seen two activities introduced.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: First, aquaculture activities taken over by Barramundi Asia Group, just beyond Bendera Bay.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I note that the Singapore Food Agency (SFA) had completed an environmental impact assessment (EIA) before implementation.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And are there any other sites around the Southern Islands which are being considered for the future?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What are the measures and safeguards which the Government requires of companies to minimise damage to the seabed, including the anchoring of cages and monitoring of feed spills?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Is there ongoing assessment as to the extent of natural habitats and water flows in both the short and medium term?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I appreciate that aquaculture is a very important part of our food resilience goals and I hope we can establish good practices and standards around it before further expansion.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Second, Big Tiny's Tiny Away Escape was launched, which will start taking bookings very soon.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Like the throngs who flocked to the Southern Islands during COVID-19, staycations were also a popular activity during COVID-19.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I think opportunities for Singaporeans to connect with nature are good, especially for our young, who are more likely to fall in love with our environment if they are familiar with it.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I echo comments from the marine community, and I sincerely appreciate the Sentosa Development Corporation's (SDC) consideration in this less intrusive accommodation option.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I also appreciate that SDC carried out stakeholder engagements and I would be keen to understand what environmental and safety considerations are required of the operator and whether any of the suggestions during consultation have been adopted.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would also appreciate hearing what the future plans are in developing the Southern Islands as a light touch ecotourism destination.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For illustration, island and land permits are currently managed by the Singapore Land Authority (SLA; the National Parks Board (NParks) is involved in conservation, for example, through the Sisters' Island Marine Park and also the conservation of heritage trees and development of trails.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While the Singapore Tourism Board (STB) looks after the development of the island into a light touch tourist destination, the Maritime Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) governs the rest of the waters that surround the island.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: A clear checklist could be developed to identify environmental considerations to be assessed before any land or sea use is approved.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Given the technicality of such environmental assessments, there is potential to crowd-in expertise and public participation through a technical work group or panel.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This would support the implementation of a well-coordinated and comprehensive plan to ensure that any development is sustainable and science-based.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I sincerely hope that the Government considers this suggestion.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How does the coastal and ecological profiling exercise by URA inform development in the Southern Islands?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In line with the plans to develop the Southern Islands sensitively, we can refer to preliminary research, horizon mapping and integrated concept plan for St John's Island developed by Dr Jani Tanzil and the team at the St John’s Island National Marine Laboratory (SJIML), funded by the National Research Foundation (NRF).

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Using participatory mapping, the team came up with a preliminary proposal of both sea and land use zonings to create an environmentally friendly multi-use space for many stakeholders.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Such zonings are in line of developing the island while ensuring that sensitive areas are kept protected.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Potential areas include education, research, tourism, religious, cultural, conservation, sea sports fishing, agriculture and even military.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With increasing developments on the island, more Singaporeans and tourists are visiting.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In nature areas such as Kranji Marshes, permits for large groups are required for similar reasons.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I hope that the Government could consider a similar concept to be rolled out on the islands.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What are some efforts made to ensure the safety of and environmentally friendly practices of visitors?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For example, there can be signs to indicate strong currents for safe enjoyment in the waters and evacuation plans in the case of emergency.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Visitors to the island will also be familiar with the long-tailed macaques which inhabit the island.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Has the Government considered how human-wildlife conflict will be minimised, especially if the families on staycation bring food and snacks with them?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would also like to know who the enforcement authority is for safety and operations on the island.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Perhaps, it will also be helpful to place life buoys at prominent locations or even consider a lifeguard during peak periods to prevent incidents of drowning.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: You have one and a half minutes left.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: Big changes can take place in the most unexpected and smallest of places.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: Let us be at the forefront as an island city-state in dealing with these issues.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: Beyond Governmental bodies, many ground-up groups and individuals have dedicated their careers and free time to this.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin
text: Let us take this step to protect what we have and ensure the sustainable development of our Southern Islands.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I only have 10 minutes, so I will be brief and may not be able to address all the questions that they have raised.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As a small city-state, we will always have to balance conservation with our development needs.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The pressures on our sea spaces are no less intense than on land.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are home to a rich array of marine biodiversity, from hard corals and seagrasses to turtles and dugongs.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Port of Singapore is also a busy global transshipment hub, supporting our economy and the continued flow of global supply chains.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our coastal and marine areas are also used for many important activities, including offshore industries, aquaculture, tourism, recreation and defence.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As we balance these competing demands, we recognise that our marine ecosystems are an important part of our natural capital and agree with Members that we must take collective action to conserve them.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Through our Marine Conservation Action Plan, we seek to conserve our rich marine biodiversity.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This comprehensive, science-based approach is part of our broader Nature Conservation Masterplan, which sets out conservation strategies for both green and blue spaces.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Over the years, NParks has been partnering experts, researchers and the marine community to study and monitor the biodiversity in our waters.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: With the use of advanced modelling tools, as well as efforts such as the Comprehensive Marine Biodiversity Survey and the more recent Southern Islands Biodiversity Survey, we continuously update and deepen our knowledge base.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This helps us to identify key marine habitats for protection.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Marine Park is protected under the Parks and Trees Act, which prohibits the removal of biodiversity and restricts activities such as fishing, the collection of corals and the mooring of boats, among others.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In addition to protecting our key marine ecosystems, we are also actively enhancing them, in close partnership with the community.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, together with JTC and the National University of Singapore (NUS), we are supporting the introduction of artificial reefs at the Marine Park, to promote the restoration of its coral habitats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We also work closely with the multi-stakeholder Friends of Marine Park, as well as volunteers, to conserve and study native turtle species at the turtle hatchery on Small Sister’s Island.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Beyond the Marine Park, we also make use of science and data to prioritise threatened species for our recovery programmes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Today, our efforts cover the Neptune’s cup sponge, over 14 species of corals, and more.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will do more to protect our natural marine habitats and heritage.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These efforts will also include coastal and marine habitats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Like Mr Louis Ng, we recognise the importance of our seagrass meadows as carbon sinks and habitats for marine fauna.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have been partnering the marine community on a long-term survey of our species-rich seagrass meadows and are currently developing a restoration programme for these habitats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And we are planning to expand our "Plant-A-Coral, Seed-A-Reef" programme to rally more of the community around our efforts to establish and restore thriving reef habitats.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will also continue to ramp up our outreach and education efforts, together with partners such as the Nature Society (Singapore) and the Waterways Watch Society.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Through initiatives such as guided intertidal walks and citizen science programmes, including our yearly Biodiversity Beach Patrols, we will encourage even more Singaporeans to join us in celebrating and stewarding our amazing marine biodiversity.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Across the board, our marine conservation efforts are underpinned by strong and active partnerships.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: One example of how ground-up efforts can make a meaningful difference is the Singapore Blue Plan, which Mr Louis Ng mentioned.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: I had the opportunity to attend the launch of the Blue Plan back in 2018 and was encouraged by the passion and dedication of the diverse stakeholders who contributed to it.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Many of our actions to better understand and conserve our marine spaces are indeed aligned with the recommendations of the Blue Plan.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For example, we are stepping up funding for marine research.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have recently started to award grants for the first two projects and we look forward to catalysing further advancements in this field.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To strengthen the environmental impact assessment (EIA) process, we are piloting the centralisation of EIA consultants under NParks.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will ensure the rigour of EIAs, including for coastal and marine areas.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And to facilitate collaboration among Government, industry and researchers in areas including marine conservation, MPA launched the GeoSpace-Sea portal in 2019.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This publicly accessible database harnesses and integrates marine and coastal geospatial data from various sources and can help parties work off a common set of information.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This also ties in with Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin’s call for greater coordination across agencies to ensure that our Southern Islands are developed sensitively.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We agree with her that proper coordination is important to ensure that we develop Singapore sustainably.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Today, we already take a whole-of-Government approach to coordinate our plans, from planning to implementation.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Upstream in the planning process, environmental considerations are taken into account in our land use plans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: URA regularly reviews our long-term plans with agencies and studies alternatives and trade-offs to optimise our land use plans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This includes working with developing agencies such as the Sentosa Development Corporation (SDC) and the Singapore Food Agency (SFA) to evaluate proposals for ecotourism projects and fish farms.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: When development plans are more firm, developing agencies undergo an in-depth consultation process and work closely with technical agencies to minimise the environmental impact for developments near or in an ecologically sensitive area.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In the context of Lazarus Island, this also involves consulting technical agencies and SLA, the agency managing the island, to develop visitor management measures that ensure public safety and sustainable practices.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Minister, you have one and a half minutes left.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are committed to being responsible stewards of our coastal and marine spaces, including our Southern Islands.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As we push on with these efforts, we encourage everyone to join us, share with us their views and ideas, to ensure that our precious marine biodiversity is conserved for many generations to come.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Pursuant to Standing Order No 2(3)(a), I wish to inform to inform hon Members that the Sitting tomorrow will commence at 10.30 am.
